newsitem.title: USA: NCR to triple size of Wal-Mart database.
newsitem.headline: NCR to triple size of Wal-Mart database.

text.p: NCR Corp said Wal-Mart Stores Inc, the world's largest retailer, had agreed to a deal in which NCR will triple the size of the already massive data warehousing system it has built for Wal-Mart.

NCR said the expanded deal calls for it to boost substantially the data analysis capabilities of Wal-Mart's data warehouse system, which it asserts will make it the largest commerical database system currently in operation.
Wal-Mart's data warehouse has information from the retailer's 2,900 stores that can be tailored by stores to give merchandise buyers insight into local purchasing patterns.

Financial terms were not disclosed. However, Yankee Group analyst Brian Murphy believed NCR stood to gain between $40 and $60 million in revenues from the expanded deal to cover new hardware, software and services it will provide.
"This is the crown jewel of NCR's Teradata club," Murphy said of the strategic importance of the Wal-Mart partnership to NCR's Teradata division.

For its own part, Wal-Mart credited its powerful data management capabilities as one it key compeitive advantages, allowing it to keep careful track of retail buying patters, store by store, shelf by shelf and day to day.
Murphy said the expansion would allow Wal-Mart to boost the amount of data it analyzes from each store, giving merchandisers greater control over purchasing decisions.
The latest Wal-Mart deal comes a month after NCR announced a similar pact to extend the data warehouse system of Reuters Holdings Plc.
In the latter pact Reuters agreed to pay NCR $50.7 million to expand its database management capacities, creating a 500 gigabyte data warehouse valued at over $76 million in total.

As part of the contract, the computer maker said it will supply one new NCR WorldMark 5100M massively parallel processing (MPP) server and upgrade a second installed NCR 5100M from 32 to 96 nodes. The new server contains 32 nodes.

Each node represents a powerful computer in its own right. In a massively parrallel system, scores of computer processors are strapped together to multiply the power of the system well beyond the sum of the power of the individual computers.
The total system contains more than 1,024 of Intel Corp's Pentium Pro 200 microprocessors.
The contract also covers NCR professional services, including database design, data transformation and data management, as well as maintenance, the company said.
The NCR WorldMark computer hardware will be installed and upgraded by mid-1997, the company said.

The two WorldMark 5100M servers -- running NCR's Teredata relational database management system (RDBMS) -- triple the size of Wal-Mart's existing data warehouse to more than 24 terabytes from 7.5 terabytes.
A terabyte equals roughly a trillion bytes of data.
